chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a group of people who prayed in congregation while they were naked (without upper garments). He said: 'The Imam should advance on his knees, and he prays with them sitting, while he himself is sitting.'

key_terms.عُرَاةٌ: Naked or lacking upper garments; plural of عاري

ai.seo_question: How should the Imam lead the prayer if the congregation is naked or lacks upper garments?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific case of 'urāh' (nakedness), distinguishing it from general nakedness by prescribing a seated prayer to maintain dignity while fulfilling the obligation. The Imam’s posture of advancing on his knees highlights the flexibility in prayer postures when physical constraints or modesty concerns require it, a nuance emphasized in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of prayer without upper garments.
